nodes.title: Invertible L_p(ξ)-sections, the formal completion and the local module
nodes.statement: Fix ξ ∈ K_3(K) and a prime p. For (m, p) = 1 let ε_m(ξ) ∈ K(ζ_m)^×/(K(ζ_m)^×)^m be the unit of HB.2 (ε_m = c_{ζ_m}^2), represented by an element that is a unit at the primes above p, and let ε_m(ξ)^{1/m} be a chosen m-th root, living in the Kummer algebra K_p[ζ_m][T]/(T^m − ε_m(ξ)), K_p = K ⊗_Q Q_p = R^_p[1/p]. An INVERTIBLE L_p(ξ)-SECTION is a family f = (f_m(x))_{m≥1,(m,p)=1} with f_m(x) ∈ ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}·(R^_p[ζ_m]^× + x R^_p[ζ_m] + x^2 K_p[ζ_m][[x]]) — constant term ε_m(ξ)^{1/m} times a unit of R^_p[ζ_m], linear coefficient integral, higher coefficients only in K_p[ζ_m]; this is the shape of GSWZ (195) and the hypothesis of Dwork's lemma; Definition 1.3 prints x K_p[ζ_m][[x]] in (20), which admits the non-integral L_p(0)-section ((1 + x/ζ_m)^{1/p})_m and makes Theorem 1 false (source issue HabiroNumberFields/E24) — such that log(φ_p f̂(q^p)/f̂(q)^p) ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} (p/x)·R^_p[ζ_m][[x]] (GSWZ (21): p divided by x, so a simple pole is allowed). Here φ_p is the Frobenius of R^_p[ζ_m] with ζ_m ↦ ζ_m^p (extension (ii) of HB.6/coefficient-rings-and-frobenius), f̂(q^p) at q = ζ_m + x is the expansion of f̂ at ζ_m^p evaluated at (ζ_m + x)^p − ζ_m^p, and the FORMAL COMPLETION f̂ is defined by log f̂_m(x) = D_p(ξ)/(m^2 log q) + log f_m(x) ∈ x^{−1}K_p[ζ_m][[x]] (GSWZ (22)), with D_p : K_3(K_p) → K_p Coleman's p-adic dilogarithm in the normalisation of PadicHodgeRegulators D.4 and log q = log(1 + x/ζ_m) (log ζ_m = 0). The LOCAL MODULE H_{R^_p,ξ} is the H_{R^_p}-span of the invertible L_p(ξ)-sections, H_{R^_p} acting componentwise. Condition (21) is the logarithmic form of the condition in Dwork's lemma (HB.7/dworks-lemma).
hypotheses: No hypothesis on p or Δ in the definition; existence (Theorem 1) needs disc(K) | Δ, 6 | Δ and p ∤ Δ (HB.7/local-freeness).

The linear coefficient must be integral (shape (195)); with the printed shape (20) the family f_m = (1 + x/ζ_m)^{1/p} has logarithmic Frobenius defect 0 but f_1 = 1 + x/p − 2x^2/p^2 + … ∉ Z_p[[x]] (PARI, p = 5), so the span of the sections would not be free of rank one.

The p/x in (21) is essential: whenever D_p(ξ) ≠ 0 the left side has x^{−1}-coefficient ζ_m(φ_p D_p(ξ) − p^2 D_p(ξ))/(p m^2) ≠ 0 (φ_p preserves valuations, so φ_p(y) = p^2 y forces y = 0); with 'p·x' in place of 'p/x' no section would exist.
The choices (the representative of ε_m(ξ) as a p-unit, its m-th root) change f_m by a unit of R^_p[ζ_m] and a root of unity; H_{R^_p,ξ} does not depend on them (API item independent_of_choices).
proofSteps: Record the Kummer algebra and the shape condition on f_m.
Define log q and 1/log q ∈ x^{−1}K_p[ζ_m][[x]], and the formal completion (22).
Define the logarithmic Frobenius defect log(φ_p f̂(q^p)/f̂(q)^p) as a Laurent series over K_p[ζ_m] and state (21).
Define H_{R^_p,ξ} as a span over H_{R^_p} (HB.6/the-p-completed-ring).

Independence of the choices: a p-unit u with ε' = ε u^m changes ε^{1/m} by u times a root of unity, which preserves the shape set and changes the Frobenius defect by log(φ_p(u)/u^p) ∈ p·R^_p[ζ_m] (u unit, φ_p(u) ≡ u^p mod p).
acceptance: For ξ = 0 (ε_m = 1, D_p(0) = 0) the constant family 1 is an invertible L_p(0)-section and H_{R^_p,0} = H_{R^_p}.
The target of (21) is (p/x)R^_p[ζ_m][[x]], not p·x·R^_p[ζ_m][[x]].
H_{R^_p,ξ} is independent of the permitted choices of ε_m(ξ) and of its m-th root.

nodes.title: Dwork's lemma and its exponential corollary
nodes.statement: Let S be p-complete and p-torsion free with a Frobenius φ_p, p ∤ m, and φ_p(ζ_m) = ζ_m^p, φ_p(x) = x. (Lemma 3.4) For f(x) ∈ 1 + xS[1/p, ζ_m][[x]]: f(x) ∈ 1 + xS[ζ_m][[x]] iff φ_p(f)((ζ_m + x)^p − ζ_m^p)/f(x)^p ∈ 1 + p x S[ζ_m][[x]] and f(x) ∈ 1 + xS[ζ_m] + O(x^2). (Corollary 3.5) If g = (g_m)_{(m,p)=1}, g_m ∈ S[1/p, ζ_m][[x]], satisfies φ_p g(q^p) − p g(q) ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} pS[ζ_m][[q − ζ_m]], then f := exp(g) is well defined, and if f(ζ_m + x) ∈ (1 + pS[ζ_m]) + xS[ζ_m] + O(x^2) then f ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} S[ζ_m][[q − ζ_m]].
hypotheses: S = R^_p for R = O_K[1/Δ], p ∤ Δ, in the applications; S[ζ_m] = S ⊗ Z[ζ_m].
The Frobenius is extension (ii) of HB.6/coefficient-rings-and-frobenius (ζ_m ↦ ζ_m^p), not extension (i).
The proof uses the finite order s of φ_p on S[ζ_m] (equation (190)); S = R^_p satisfies this since R^_p[ζ_m] is finite étale over Z_p.
proofSteps: If the coefficients a_k are integral the quotient is ≡ 1 mod p (186).
Conversely compare coefficients in (187)-(188) to get a_n − ζ_m^{p−1} n p^{...}φ_p(a_n) ∈ S[ζ_m] (189); average over the s-fold iterate of φ_p (190) and induct on n.
Corollary: (192) gives g_m(0) ∈ pS[ζ_m], so exp converges; (194) and Lemma 3.4 give integrality.
acceptance: For f = 1 + px both sides hold; for f = 1 + x/p the quotient condition fails.
The exponential of a Dwork-type logarithm with constant term in pS is integral.

nodes.title: The Dwork-type difference of the infinite Pochhammer symbol
nodes.statement: (Lemma 2.1) For every integer n and prime p, Li_n^{(p)}(t) := Σ_{k≥1, p∤k} t^k/k^n lies in Z[t, 1/(1−t)]^_p. (Proposition 2.2) (a) log(t^p; q^p)_∞ − p log(t; q)_∞ ∈ (p/x)·Z[t, 1/(1−t)]^_p[[x]] for q = 1 + x. (b) For a root of unity ζ ∈ C_p ∖ {1} of order not a power of p, log(ζ^p; q^p)_∞ − p log(ζ; q)_∞ ∈ p Li_2^{(p)}(ζ)/x + pZ_{(p)}[ζ][[x]], a meromorphic function on |x| < 1 with a simple pole at x = 0 and the residue shown.

Part (b) specialises (a) along t ↦ ζ, which is compatible with the Frobenius t ↦ t^p.

(a) from the expansion (48) of the difference, Lemma 2.1 and Z[t, 1/(1−t)]^_p[1/p] ∩ Z_{(p)}[[t]] ⊆ Z[t, 1/(1−t)]^_p (57).
(b) by the specialisation (58).

nodes.title: Explicit invertible sections from the infinite Pochhammer symbol
nodes.statement: Let p > 3 be unramified in K. For ζ ∈ μ(K_p) put Ψ_{[ζ],p,m}(x) := exp(−Li_2(ζ)/(m^2 log q)) ε_m([ζ])^{1/m} (q^{m/2}ζ; q^m)_∞^{1/m} for (m,p) = 1 and q = ζ_m + x, an element of ε_m([ζ])^{1/m}(1 + xK_p[ζ_m][[x]]) (Definition 3.9). For ξ̂ = Σ_ζ a_ζ[ζ] ∈ K_3(K_p) ⊗ Z_p (a presentation of the image of ξ ∈ K_3(K), which exists by Theorem 9, PadicHodgeRegulators D.3) put Ψ_{ξ̂,p} := ∏_ζ Ψ_{[ζ],p}^{a_ζ}. Then Ψ_{ξ̂,p} is an invertible L_p(ξ̂)-section (Theorem 10), and its class in H_{R^_p,ξ}^×/H_{R^_p}^× depends only on ξ̂, not on the presentation (Corollary 3.10).
hypotheses: p > 3 unramified in K (p ∤ Δ with disc(K) | Δ and 6 | Δ).
ξ̂ is in the image of K_3(K) → K_3(K_p; Z_p) ⊗ Z_p; the Z_p-exponents a_ζ are made sense of p-adically.
ε_m([ζ]) is the unit of HB.2 for the symbol [ζ]; D_p([ζ]) = Li_2(ζ) for ζ ∈ μ(K_p) with the normalisation of D.4.

With Definition 1.3 corrected to the shape (195), Theorem 10 also needs the linear coefficient of Ψ_{[ζ],p,m} to be p-integral; the source's proof ('a slight variation of Proposition 2.2 … and equation (56)') does not address it, so this is part of the gap on the proofs of Theorems 1 and 10.
proofSteps: Define Ψ_{[ζ],p} and check the shape (207).
Theorem 10: combine HB.7/pochhammer-dwork-difference (b), with the factor q^{1/2}, and the level-m decomposition (59) to verify (21).
Extend multiplicatively to Z_p-combinations using convergence of the p-adic powers.
Corollary 3.10: two presentations give sections whose quotient is an L_p(0)-section, hence in H_{R^_p}^× (HB.7/dworks-lemma).
acceptance: Ψ_{[ζ],p} is an L_p([ζ])-section for p > 3 unramified.
The class of Ψ_{ξ̂,p} modulo H_{R^_p}^× is independent of the presentation.

nodes.title: Invertible sections exist and the local modules are free of rank one (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and Δ divisible by disc(K) and by 6. For ξ ∈ K_3(K) and every prime p ∤ Δ, invertible L_p(ξ)-sections exist, and H_{R^_p,ξ} is a FREE H_{R^_p}-module of rank one, generated by any invertible L_p(ξ)-section.
hypotheses: 6 | Δ excludes p = 2, 3, where Lemma 3.6 and the regulator theorem fail (Remark 1.8).
Definition 1.3 is read with the shape (195) (linear coefficient integral); with the printed shape (20) the theorem is false already for ξ = 0 (HB.7/invertible-local-sections, test q_power_excluded).
p ∤ Δ makes p unramified and p > 3.
The statement is local at p; no global freeness follows (HB.7/what-the-local-picture-does-not-give).
proofSteps: Existence: HB.7/pochhammer-sections gives Ψ_{ξ̂,p} (Theorem 10 with Theorem 9 of D.3), alternatively the telescoping construction (209)-(210).

Freeness: if f, g are invertible L_p(ξ)-sections then h = g/f is an invertible L_p(0)-section with integral linear coefficient; its logarithmic Frobenius defect is a power series lying in (p/x)R^_p[ζ_m][[x]], hence in pR^_p[ζ_m][[x]]; after multiplying by the constant unit family (h_m(0)^{−1})_m ∈ H_{R^_p}^×, HB.7/dworks-lemma (Corollary 3.5) gives h, h^{−1} ∈ H_{R^_p}. So every section is a unit multiple of f, and the span is H_{R^_p}·f, free because every f_m is invertible in the Kummer algebra over K_p[ζ_m][[x]].
acceptance: ξ = 0: H_{R^_p,0} = H_{R^_p}, generated by 1.
The rank is one and the module is free, for every p ∤ Δ.
Nothing is claimed for p | 6.

sources.excerpt: Theorem 1. Let K be a number field, and ∆ a number divisible by its discriminant and by 6. For ξ ∈ K3(K) and p a prime with (p, ∆) = 1, there exists invertible Lp(ξ)-sections. Moreover, HR∧p,ξ is a free rank 1 module over HR∧p.

nodes.title: Extending an invertible section to all roots of unity
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.6) Fix p, ξ and a family f = (f_m)_{m≥1} with f_m ∈ ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}(R^_p[ζ_m]^× + xR^_p[ζ_m] + x^2K_p[ζ_m][[x]]) satisfying φ_p f̂(q^p)/f̂(q)^p ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} exp((p/x)R^_p[ζ_m][[x]]). Then for each m prime to p there is a unique β_m ∈ Z_p such that f̃_{mp^d}(x) := ζ_{p^d}^{β_m} f_{mp^d}(x) satisfies f̃(q^σ)/f̃(q)^{σ^{−1}} ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} R^_p[ζ_m][[x]] for all σ ∈ Z_p^×. (Corollary 3.7) An invertible L_p(ξ)-section has a unique extension to all roots of unity satisfying these integrality and gluing conditions.
hypotheses: p ≠ 2, 3: the proof needs a root of unity ω ∈ Z_p^× with ω − ω^{−1} ∈ Z_p^×, equivalently some γ prime to p with γ^2 − 1 prime to p.
Used in the proof of Theorem 2 (H_{R,0} = H_R).
proofSteps: Compare f(q^σ) with f(q)^σ using (198) and Dwork's lemma, inductively on d.
The cocycle α_{σσ'} = σ'α_σ + σ^{−1}α_{σ'} (201) has the unique solution α_σ = (σ − σ^{−1})α_ω/(ω − ω^{−1}) (202); β_m = −α_ω/(ω − ω^{−1}).

nodes.title: The Habiro module H_{R,ξ} of a class in K₃(K)
nodes.statement: Fix ξ ∈ K_3(K). The H_R-module H_{R,ξ} consists of the families f = (f_m(x))_{m≥1} with f_m(x) ∈ ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}·K[ζ_m][[x]] (rational coefficients; integrality comes only from the conditions) such that (1) for every prime p ∤ Δ, the image of (f_m)_{(m,p)=1} under K → K_p LIES IN THE LOCAL MODULE H_{R^_p,ξ} (the span of the invertible sections — elements of H_{R,ξ} need not be invertible sections, e.g. 0 and p·f), and (2) for every γ ∈ Z_{>0}, the PRODUCT f(q^γ)^γ · f(q^{−1}) lies in the restricted ring H_{R[1/γ]}|γ of the LOCALISATION R[1/γ] (GSWZ (24)). Here f(q^γ) and f(q^{−1}) at q = ζ_m + x, (m, γ) = 1, are the expansions of f at ζ_m^γ and ζ_m^{−1}; they are defined up to the choice of m-th roots of the Galois-conjugate units, and the χ^{−1}-equivariance of ε_m (σ_γ(ε_m(ξ))^γ/ε_m(ξ) is canonically an m-th power) makes the product in (24) independent of these choices. The condition (24) needs no meaning for ξ/γ; that issue concerns the separate operation γ* (HB.7/operations-on-the-modules). H_R acts componentwise and preserves both conditions; closure under ADDITION is not routine, because (24) is not additive in f, and it is part of HB.7/the-ring-case-and-tensor-products. For γ ≥ 1 the restricted module H_{R,ξ}|γ uses only orders prime to γ; H_{R,ξ}|Δ is the target of GSWZ Theorem 5.
hypotheses: disc(K) | Δ and 6 | Δ. The local condition is imposed for every prime p ∤ Δ; for p | Δ, R^_p = 0 and GSWZ's identification K_p = R^_p[1/p] = K ⊗ Q_p (19) fails (the left side is 0), so the condition must be read as void there (Definition 1.4 leaves p unquantified; source issue HabiroNumberFields/E28). p = 2, 3 are inverted so that (24) determines the local gluing (HB.7/extension-to-all-roots).
ε_m(ξ) and the χ^{−1}-equivariance datum are HB.2's exported interface; D_p(ξ) enters only through the local condition.
H_{R,ξ}|Δ in GSWZ §1.7 is printed as satisfying '(13)'; the intended conditions are those of Definition 1.4 on orders prime to Δ (source issue HabiroNumberFields/E25).
proofSteps: Define the ambient ∏_m ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}K[ζ_m][[x]] inside ∏_m KummerAlg_m[[x]].
State the local condition through K[ζ_m] → K_p[ζ_m] and HB.7/invertible-local-sections.
Define the expansions f(q^γ), f(q^{−1}) and state (24) in H_{R[1/γ]}|γ (HB.6/the-gluing-condition for the ring R[1/γ]).
Show independence of the choices of m-th roots of the conjugate units, using χ^{−1}-equivariance.

Check stability under multiplication by H_R: the local condition because H_R → H_{R^_p}, and (24) because (af)(q^γ)^γ(af)(q^{−1}) = a(q^γ)^γ a(q^{−1})·f(q^γ)^γ f(q^{−1}) with the first factor in H_{R[1/γ]}|γ. Closure under addition is deferred to HB.7/the-ring-case-and-tensor-products.
acceptance: The local condition is membership in the span H_{R^_p,ξ}, so H_{R,ξ} is an H_R-submodule containing 0.
Condition (24) is a product condition in H_{R[1/γ]}|γ.
For ξ = 0, H_{R,0} = H_R (HB.7/the-ring-case-and-tensor-products).

nodes.title: H_{R,0} = H_R, and multiplication H_{R,ξ} ⊗ H_{R,ξ'} ≅ H_{R,ξ+ξ'} (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: (0) H_{R,ξ} is closed under addition, hence an H_R-module: at each p ∤ Δ an element is a·s̃ on all orders, with s̃ the extension (Corollary 3.7) of an invertible section and a ∈ H_{R^_p}, and (24) can be checked prime by prime; the source gives no argument for this (gap). (1) H_{R,0} = H_R. (2) Multiplication of families defines an H_R-bilinear map H_{R,ξ} × H_{R,ξ'} → H_{R,ξ+ξ'}, and GSWZ Theorem 2 asserts that the induced map H_{R,ξ} ⊗_{H_R} H_{R,ξ'} → H_{R,ξ+ξ'} is a canonical isomorphism, so that each H_{R,ξ} is an invertible H_R-module and ξ ↦ H_{R,ξ} is a homomorphism K_3(K) → Pic(H_R) (to line bundles, not only to isomorphism classes). The printed proof establishes (1) and the well-definedness of the multiplication map; it does not show that the tensor map is surjective or injective, nor that H_{R,ξ} is non-zero for arbitrary ξ (gap 'Theorem 2 beyond the multiplication map' and source issue HabiroNumberFields/E23).

nodes.title: The operations γ* and τ, restriction of orders, and what GSWZ does not prove
nodes.statement: For γ ∈ Z ∖ {0} the operation γ* on P_R is (γ*f)(q) := f(q^γ): at q = ζ_m + x its component is the expansion of f at ζ_m^γ evaluated at (ζ_m + x)^γ − ζ_m^γ, a power series with zero constant term, so this is an honest substitution (Mathlib's PowerSeries.subst applies). τ := (−1)* is f(q) ↦ f(q^{−1}). Proven properties (GSWZ Proposition 1.5): (a) f ∈ H_{R,ξ} ⇒ τf ∈ H_{R,−ξ}; (c) (γγ')*f = γ*(γ'*f) for f ∈ P_R; (d) f ∈ H_{R,ξ}, γ > 0 ⇒ (γ*f)^γ ∈ H_{R[1/γ],ξ}|γ. The source states that γ*f 'behaves like' an element of H_{R[1/γ],ξ/γ}|γ but does not define ξ/γ; no such statement is made here. Restriction of orders H_{R,ξ} → H_{R,ξ}|γ is HB.7/the-global-module's. Multiplication is HB.7/the-ring-case-and-tensor-products. EXTENSION OF SCALARS along a finite étale R → R', a GALOIS ACTION on the modules, and compatibility of the Frobenius gluing with the K_3 TRANSFER are asked for by the stage text but are NOT stated or proved in GSWZ; they are recorded as a gap, not claimed.
hypotheses: (a) and (d) use the χ^{−1}-equivariance of ε_m; (c) is formal.
Only γ with the stated signs and the localisation R[1/γ] are covered.
No hypothesis-free scalar extension, Galois action or transfer compatibility is asserted.
proofSteps: Define γ* componentwise through the Galois action σ_γ on R[ζ_m] (ζ_m ↦ ζ_m^γ) and substitution of (ζ_m + x)^γ − ζ_m^γ; define τ.
(c) from the definition.
(a) and (d) from χ^{−1}-equivariance: the constant terms of τf and (γ*f)^γ carry ε_m(ξ)^{−1/m} and ε_m(ξ)^{1/m} up to canonical m-th powers, and conditions (21), (24) transform accordingly.
Record the three operations the source does not treat as a gap.
acceptance: τ is an involution of P_R mapping H_{R,ξ} to H_{R,−ξ}.
(γγ')* = γ* ∘ γ'* on P_R.
(γ*f)^γ ∈ H_{R[1/γ],ξ}|γ for f ∈ H_{R,ξ}.
Scalar extension, Galois action and transfer compatibility are not claimed.

nodes.title: Invertible does not mean free, and multiplication by an element need not be an isomorphism
nodes.statement: The local modules H_{R^_p,ξ} are FREE of rank one (Theorem 1) and, by Theorem 2 as stated, the global modules are invertible (rank one, locally free), and the tensor multiplication H_{R,ξ} ⊗ H_{R,ξ'} → H_{R,ξ+ξ'} is an isomorphism. Two things do NOT follow: (1) H_{R,ξ} need not be free (GSWZ: 'not necessarily free'); freeness is known in the abelian case only for ξ = Σ n_j[ζ^j] Galois-invariant, with generator ∏_j (q^{1/2}ζ^j; q)_∞^{n_j}, a claim the source does not prove (source issue HabiroNumberFields/E26). (2) Multiplication by a single element, g ↦ gf from H_R to H_{R,ξ}, is an isomorphism only when f generates H_{R,ξ}; e.g. for ξ = 0, f = 1 − q ∈ H_Z, g ↦ (1 − q)g is injective but not surjective, since 1 − q is not a unit (its value at q = 1 is 0). Any global statement cites a global theorem (Theorem 2, or a freeness theorem), never the local description.
hypotheses: Theorem 2's isomorphism is carried with the gap recorded at HB.7/the-ring-case-and-tensor-products.
Invertible = finitely generated projective of rank one; free would mean isomorphic to H_R.
proofSteps: State Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 with their hypotheses.
(1): no source proves freeness in general; record the abelian claim and its missing proof.
(2): the example 1 − q: H_Z is a domain, so multiplication is injective; 1 is not in the image because ev_1((1 − q)g) = 0.
Export the rule: global statements cite global theorems.
acceptance: H_{R^_p,ξ} is free of rank one; H_{R,ξ} is invertible (Theorem 2 as stated) but not claimed free.
g ↦ (1 − q)g on H_Z is not surjective.
The tensor multiplication map is not listed as a counterexample: Theorem 2 asserts it is an isomorphism.

gaps.title: The Galois-module structure of the units (Herbrand's unit theorem)
gaps.detail: For a Galois extension L/K of number fields with group G, O_Lˣ ⊗ ℂ ⊕ ℂ ≅ ⊕_{v | ∞ of K} ℂ[G/G_w]. CGZ Proposition 2.12 derives its statement from this (their proof says 'From the proof of Dirichlet's unit theorem'). Mathlib has Dirichlet's theorem (NumberField.Units.rank) but not the equivariant form, and no roadmap plans it. NEXT ACTION: route to the roadmap that owns the analytic class number formula or Dirichlet's theorem (a Tau Ceti number-theory roadmap, or ArithmeticKTheory N.1's units node). Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: The Kashaev–Mangazeev–Stroganov identity is quoted, not proved
gaps.detail: CGZ prove the five-term relation for R_ζ from equation (C.7) of Kashaev–Mangazeev–Stroganov, Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 8 (1993) 1399–1409, which is not on the arXiv and was not read; the alternative cyclic-algebra proof of Gangl and Kontsevich (CGZ Remark 1.9) is unpublished. The identity as CGZ quote it was checked exactly (all n^3 root choices in F_{q^2} for n ≤ 11, and over C to 1e−74 for n ≤ 9), so the statement is right; the proof is missing. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain KMS 1993, Appendix C, or write a direct proof (both sides are rational functions of x, y subject to one relation). Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: The identification of Hutchinson's bar-cycle element with the Bloch-group element η_ζ
gaps.detail: Hutchinson defines η_ζ in K_3(Q(ζ)^+)/N as the image of [α_3(t_ζ)] and identifies it with CGZ's (34) through the formula of Hutchinson, 'A Bloch–Wigner complex for SL_2', J. K-Theory 12 (2013), §6.4, for the image of H_3 of a cyclic subgroup of SL_2(F) in RP(F) → P(F). That paper was not read. The two Bloch-group expressions were checked to agree as multisets (n ≤ 11), but the sign and normalisation of the map H_3(SL_2(F), Z) → B(F) against Suslin's map (K3BlochGroups:V.4) are not established here. The same source is the open K3BlochGroups gap 'The finite-field inputs of CGZ §4.2 beyond Suslin's sequence are unowned', whose neededBy names HabiroNumberFields:HB.2. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: The sign of the comparison scalar
gaps.detail: Hutchinson's Lemma 4.1 writes −c̄_{1,1}(x) ∪ c̄_{1,0}(β) = −x ∪ ζ = x ⊗ ζ; with c̄_{1,1} the Kummer map (his §2.3) and c̄_{1,0}(β) = ζ (his §4; Weibel V.11.10.1) the middle term is −(x ⊗ ζ), so as printed the computation gives c_ζ(η_ζ) = ζ^{−1} and R_ζ = c_ζ^{−2}. Whether another convention (the sign of Soulé's c̄_{1,1}, CGZ's Chern class versus Soulé's, Suslin's map, Hutchinson 2013) compensates is not settled by either paper; CGZ's conjecture is itself 'up to sign'. Soulé 1979 (Invent. Math. 55) was not accessible (publisher paywall; the EuDML record served no text). NEXT SOURCE ACTION: read Soulé 1979 §§II.2–II.3 for the sign conventions of c_{i,k} and of the product formula, and fix the convention in chern-sign-conventions. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: No source proof of the p-adic splitting (14) of the classical ring
gaps.detail: GSWZ (14) asserts Z_p[q]^N ≅ ∏_{(m,p)=1} Z_p[ζ_m][[q − ζ_m]] ('because there are no gluing constraints between the expansions around different roots of unity of order prime to p') without proof, and GSWZ §1.3 attributes the gluing description of the image of Z[q]^N to Habiro [27], which proves only injectivity. The node HB.6/the-p-adic-classical-ring carries a proof sketch (Chinese remainder over Z_p, (p, Φ_m)-adic completion, Hensel) that no source in the packet contains. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: read Wagner, arXiv 2410.23078v5 §2.1, and Scholze, 'Canonical q-deformations in arithmetic geometry' §§ on the Habiro ring, for a published proof; otherwise have the sketch checked as the packet's own. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: Theorem 2 beyond the multiplication map
gaps.detail: The printed proof of GSWZ Theorem 2 (§3.3) proves H_{R,0} = H_R and that multiplication maps H_{R,ξ} × H_{R,ξ'} into H_{R,ξ+ξ'}. It does not prove (i) that H_{R,ξ} is closed under addition (Definition 1.4 calls it a module, but (24) is not additive in f), (ii) that H_{R,ξ} ⊗_{H_R} H_{R,ξ'} → H_{R,ξ+ξ'} is surjective or injective, or (iii) that H_{R,ξ} ≠ 0 for arbitrary ξ (for ξ' = −ξ surjectivity needs Σ f_i g_i = 1). Global elements are constructed only for ξ from Nahm data (Theorem 5, in H_{R[δ^{−1/2}],ξ}|Δ). NEXT SOURCE ACTION: look for a proof of invertibility by patching (the abstract definition of H_R by gluing base changes along Frobenius twists, §1.4) in a later version or in Wagner's thesis; until then the tensor isomorphism and K_3(K) → Pic(H_R) are carried as conditional. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: Scalar extension, Galois action and transfer compatibility have no source
gaps.detail: The HB.7 stage text asks for extension of scalars, the Galois action and the compatibility of the Frobenius gluing with the K_3 transfer 'with exactly the invertibility/localisation hypotheses proved in GSWZ'. GSWZ states and proves none of these (the only Galois statements are Remark 1.9 about √δ and the Galois invariance of P_R; there is no transfer). The packet's operations node asserted all three. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: find a source (HabiroRings HR.6 plans 'the scalar-extension and Picard comparisons'), or plan the statements as this roadmap's own with full proofs. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: Theorem 10 and the corrected shape of invertible sections
gaps.detail: Theorem 10 is proved in one sentence ('A slight variation of Proposition 2.2 of Section 2.1 and equation (56), to include the factor of q^{1/2}'). After Definition 1.3 is corrected to the shape (195) (linear coefficient integral, source issue HabiroNumberFields/E5), Theorem 10 also needs the linear coefficient of Ψ_{[ζ],p,m} to be p-integral, which the source does not check. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: carry out the variation of Proposition 2.2 with the factor q^{m/2} and the level-m decomposition (59), or use the telescoping construction (209)-(210), whose shape can be controlled directly. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

gaps.title: CGZ Theorem 7.4, R_ζ(η_ζ) = ζ², is proved only through Nahm-sum asymptotics
gaps.detail: Hutchinson deduces R_ζ = c_ζ² from his c_ζ(η_ζ) = ζ and CGZ Theorem 7.4, R_ζ(η_ζ) = ζ². CGZ prove Theorem 7.4 (§7.2) through the radial asymptotics of Nahm sums (Theorem 7.1) and the Andrews–Gordon identity, which HabiroNahmSeries HB.4 plans (HB.4/acceptance-andrews-gordon); that stage requires HabiroNumberFields HB.2, so the input cannot be a prerequisite here without a stage cycle. It was checked numerically (locally for odd n ≤ 27 and globally for n = 5). NEXT ACTION: accept the restructure entry placing the final equality after HabiroNahmSeries HB.4, or find a proof of Theorem 7.4 that avoids Nahm sums. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.

requests.need: Graded-commutative products K_n(A; Z/N) × K_m(A; Z/N) → K_{n+m}(A; Z/N) for N odd and commutative A, compatible with the Hurewicz maps h_n : K_n(A; Z/N) → H_n(GL(A), Z/N), where the product on homology is induced by the tensor product of matrices (the Pontryagin product on H_*(GL_1(A), Z/N)).

GSWZ §5.1 for R = Z[1/Δ] and Z_p: the finite-level maps ι^N : R[q]/((q;q)_{N−1}) → P_R^N are given by an integer matrix M_N independent of R, injective with non-zero determinant (graded pieces D_{m,ℓ} = m^{2ℓ−1}(ℓ − 1)!, (310)-(311)), and Proposition 5.2: H ∈ ι(R[q]^N) iff M_N^* applied to its coordinates is ≡ 0 mod D(N) for all N. PLAN-HABIRO places GSWZ §5.1 in HC.4 (recorded as remaining by REV-HabiroCyclotomicCompletions).
Gabber rigidity in the form K_3(O_{F,q}; Z_p) ≅ K_3(F_q) ⊗ Z_p for the completion O_{F,q} of the ring of integers at a prime q not above p (CGZ proof of Lemma 4.1).

For a number field F, n = p^m and a prime q of F not above p: the étale Chern class K_3(F)/n → H^1(F, Z/n(2)) is compatible with completion at q and lands, on K_3(O_F) = K_3(F), in the unramified classes identified with H^1(F_q, Z/n(2)); with the finite-field Chern class c_{ζ,q} on K_3(F_q)/n (CGZ Lemma 4.1).

The finite and continuous Tate twists ℤ/n(m) = μ_n^{⊗m} and ℤ_p(m) = lim μ_{p^k}^{⊗m}, with the Galois action through χ^m, and ℚ_p/ℤ_p(m) (whose invariants define w_m(F)), as used in CGZ §3.1. The RS-10 link M.1 → HB.1 records this dependence.

Tate's theorem in the field form K_2(F)/n ≅ H^2(F, Z/n(2)) and the n-torsion statement K_2(F)[n] ≅ H^2(F, Z_p(2))[n] for n = p^m, used in CGZ (38) to show R_ζ : B(F; Z/n) → H^1(F, Z/n(2)) is an isomorphism for n prime to w_2(F).

The degree-three case at odd primes of the comparison with Galois cohomology. For a number field F and an odd prime p: Soulé's Chern class gives K₃(F) ⊗ ℤ_p ≅ K₃(O_F) ⊗ ℤ_p ≅ H¹_ét(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(2)), and H¹_ét(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(2)) ≅ H¹(F, ℤ_p(2)) (CGZ Theorem 3.2 and §3.2). For a number field E ⊇ μ_N with N odd: c̄_{2,1} : K₃(E; ℤ/N) → H¹(E, μ_N^{⊗2}) is an isomorphism (Hutchinson Theorem 2.10, Levine's theorem, in this case). The HB.1 stage requires M.7; the packet had omitted it.

Soulé's étale Chern classes c̄_{i,k} : K_{2i−k}(A; ℤ/ℓ^ν) → H^k(A, μ_{ℓ^ν}^{⊗i}) for rings A with ℓ invertible, and their ℓ-adic limits c : K_{2m−1}(F) → H¹(F, ℤ_ℓ(m)). Needed with: compatibility with reduction modulo ℓ^ν and with K_m(A)/ℓ^ν → K_m(A; ℤ/ℓ^ν); base change along finite extensions; c̄_{1,1} = the Kummer map on K₁(F; ℤ/N) = Fˣ/(Fˣ)^N; and Soulé's product formula (Hutchinson Theorem 2.12, Soulé II.3 Théorème 1(i)) with its specialisation c̄_{2,1}(a∗b) = −c̄_{1,1}(a) ∪ c̄_{1,0}(b) (Hutchinson Corollary 2.13).

GSWZ Theorem 9: for p > 3 unramified, D_p : K_3(K_p; Z_p) → p^2 O_{K_p} is a Z_p-linear isomorphism and K_3(K_p; Z_p) is generated by the classes [ζ], ζ ∈ μ(K_p). Used for the presentation (206) of ξ̂ in the proof of Theorem 1.

The localisation map K_3(K) → K_3(K_p; Z_p) for p unramified and the p-adic regulator D_p : K_3(K_p) → K_p = K ⊗ Q_p in the exact normalisation of GSWZ (19) and (22) (Coleman's p-adic dilogarithm D_p(z) = Li_2(z) + ½ log z log(1 − z), with D_p([ζ]) = Li_2(ζ) for roots of unity), with its compatibility with Frobenius (D_p(φ_p ξ) = φ_p D_p(ξ)).

E/m as the cofiber of multiplication by m on a spectrum and the Bockstein exact sequence 0 → π_n(E)/m → π_n(E/m) → π_{n−1}(E)[m] → 0, applied to the K-theory spectrum. This gives K_m(R; ℤ/ℓ) and 0 → K_m(R)/ℓ → K_m(R; ℤ/ℓ) → K_{m−1}(R)[ℓ] → 0 (Hutchinson §2.3). It replaces the request to StableHomotopyKTheory:H.2, which supplies none of this.

The Chebotarev density theorem: for a finite Galois extension of number fields and a conjugacy class C of its Galois group, the primes with Frobenius class C have Dirichlet density #C/#G, in particular are infinite; used with Frobenius prescribed simultaneously in a cyclotomic field and a Kummer extension (CGZ Proposition 4.2 and proof of Theorem 5.2). A Tau Ceti layer cannot be a node prerequisite, hence this request.

Inflation–restriction 0 → H¹(G/N, M^N) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M) for a closed normal subgroup N of a profinite group G and a discrete module M (explicitInfl1_injective, explicitInfRes_exact), applied to G_{F_n} ⊂ G_F with M = ℤ/n(m).

Hilbert 90 for the separable closure and the Kummer isomorphism Lˣ/(Lˣ)^n ≅ H¹(G_L, μ_n) for n invertible in L. Tau Ceti has the injective Kummer map TauCeti.kummerClassMap_injective; surjectivity is this layer's. Used for H¹(F_n, μ_n) = F_nˣ/(F_nˣ)^n in CGZ §3.1. The RS-10 link records this dependence.

restructure.title: HB.1's Bloch-convention comparison is K3BlochGroups V.3/V.6's; HB.1's stage text should say so and name its real inputs
restructure.detail: The HB.1 stage text says 'Compare CGZ's Bloch group with V's Suslin convention. Define the actual maps and identify the bounded 2-/6-primary differences'. K3BlochGroups:V.3/cgz-convention-comparison (accepted) does exactly that, and finds kernel and cokernel elementary abelian 2-groups. The stage text also says 'χ^{−1}-eigenspace in cyclotomic units', but CGZ's eigenspaces are in the units and power classes of the cyclotomic extension F_n = F(ζ). Finally, the HB.1 stage `requires` N.5, V.4 and M.7, but its inputs also include M.8 (Chern classes), M.1 (twists) and Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology layers 5 and 9 (RS-10 links M.1 and layer 9 to HB.1). RS-10's 'keep' of 'Bloch/Suslin conventions' in HB.1 conflicts with the accepted K3BlochGroups ownership. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.
restructure.proposal: HB.1 stage text: replace the first two sentences by 'Import the Bloch conventions and their comparison κ (kernel and cokernel elementary abelian 2-groups) from K3BlochGroups V.3, and the identification K₃(F)/n ≅ B_CGZ(F)/n for odd n prime to w_F from V.6; no integral identification.' Replace 'χ^{−1}-eigenspace in cyclotomic units' by 'χ^{−1}-eigenspace of the units (and power classes) of F_n = F(ζ_n)'. Add MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.8 and M.1 to HB.1's requires.

restructure.title: Hutchinson's refinement cannot be closed inside HB.2: add a stage HB.2b after HabiroNahmSeries:HB.4
restructure.detail: R_ζ = c_ζ^2 is deduced from Hutchinson's c_ζ(η_ζ) = ζ AND CGZ Theorem 7.4, R_ζ(η_ζ) = ζ^2 (Hutchinson §1: 'One of the main results of their paper is that R_ζ(η_ζ)=ζ^2 ... from which it follows that R_ζ=c_ζ^2'). Theorem 7.4 is proved only through the radial asymptotics of Nahm sums (CGZ §7.2 via Theorem 7.1), which HabiroNahmSeries:HB.4 owns (node HB.4/acceptance-andrews-gordon), and HabiroNahmSeries:HB.4's nodes cyclic-dilogarithm-interface and simplified-form-and-the-unit require HabiroNumberFields:HB.2. An HB.2 node citing HB.4/acceptance-andrews-gordon therefore closes a stage cycle HB.2 → HN:HB.4 → HB.2. Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.
restructure.proposal: New stage HabiroNumberFields:HB.2b 'Hutchinson's refinement', requires HabiroNumberFields:HB.2 and HabiroNahmSeries:HB.4; it holds the single node HB.2b/hutchinson-refinement (R_ζ = c_ζ^2 for n prime to M_F, hence ε_m = R_{ζ_m} for m prime to M_K). Consumers: HabiroNahmSeries:HB.9 (node constant-term-is-the-unit, GSWZ's use of 'Theorem 1.6 ... combined with Hutchinson') and HabiroNumberFields:KU-finitereg. HB.2 keeps CGZ Theorem 1.6 (R_ζ = c_ζ^γ, γ invertible and field-independent), Hutchinson's Theorem 3.1 and the conditional scalar-from-eta. HB.7 does not need HB.2b: it uses ε_m = c^2 by definition.

restructure.title: HB.2 stage text: the 'weaker comparison outside the refinement' is vacuous, the exported units are c^2 for every m, and Soulé's formula is imported
restructure.detail: (1) For a number field, (n, w_F) = 1 forces n odd, and n prime to M_F (the hypothesis of CGZ Theorem 1.6) implies n odd and μ_n(F) = 1; so there is no n for which Theorem 1.6 holds but Hutchinson's hypotheses fail, and 'outside the refinement's hypotheses retain the source's weaker comparison' has no content. Conversely Hutchinson states R_ζ = c_ζ^2 for all odd N with μ_N(F) = 1 but proves it through Theorem 1.6, i.e. for n prime to M_F. (2) GSWZ (16) defines ε_m = c^2_{ζ_m} on K_3(K) for every m ≥ 1, including m with μ_m ⊂ K where R_ζ does not exist; 'the units ε_m(ξ)' of the stage text must be these. (3) 'Construct ... Soulé's Chern-product formula' duplicates MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.8 ('Prove compatibility with ... products'). Added by REV-HabiroNumberFields.
restructure.proposal: Replace the second paragraph's last two sentences by: 'This does not set the scalar to one. CGZ's comparison and the refinement are both stated for n prime to M_F, which forces n odd and μ_n(F) = 1; for other n no comparison between R_ζ and c_ζ is available and none is used. The sign of the scalar depends on the conventions for the Kummer map and the Chern class, which are fixed explicitly.' Replace 'Construct cyclic bar cycles, the Bott element and Soulé's Chern-product formula' by 'Construct cyclic bar cycles and the Bott element, and specialise Soulé's Chern-product formula (imported from MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8) to degree three with its sign.' Replace the first sentence of the third paragraph by: 'The interface exported to GSWZ is ε_m(ξ) = c_{ζ_m}(ξ)^2 for ξ ∈ K_3(K) and every m ≥ 1, as a χ^{-1}-class of K(ζ_m)^×/m unramified away from m, with its Kummer class, its root line, χ^{-1}-equivariance, multiplicativity and coherence under m | m'; for m prime to M_K it equals R_{ζ_m} of the Bloch class.'

restructure.detail: (1) HabiroNahmSeries:HB.4/cyclic-dilogarithm-interface defines D_ζ(x) = ∏(1 − ζ^t x)^t (CGZ's normalisation) and states D_ζ(1)^{24m} = m^{12m}; in that normalisation D_ζ(1)^{24} = m^{12m} and D_ζ(1)^{24m} ≠ m^{12m} for m ≥ 2 (PARI/GP, m = 2..16). sourceIssues.locator: §3.1, the sentence before (29), p. 18 (arXiv v3; checked on the rendered page)
sourceIssues.printed: A choice of primitive nth root of unity ζ gives a trivialization t_ζ : Z/nZ(1) =_ζ Z/nZ(m) defined by sending ζ to ζ^{⊗n}.
sourceIssues.correction: … defined by sending ζ to ζ^{⊗m}.
sourceIssues.reason: t_ζ lands in ℤ/n(m) = μ_n^{⊗m}, so the image of ζ is its m-th tensor power. With ζ ↦ ζ^{⊗m}: t_{ζ^k}(ζ^k) = k^m ζ^{⊗m} and t_ζ(ζ^k) = k ζ^{⊗m}, giving the printed t_{ζ^k} = k^{m−1}t_ζ and (29) with χ^{1−m}. With ⊗n neither formula holds.

review.notes: Independent review of all 18 nodes, the baseline, the requests, gaps, coverage and restructure entries, and the suggested Lean file, by three checkers (HB.1 with the baseline, the library audit and the K-theory suppliers; HB.2 with Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier and Hutchinson; HB.6–HB.7 with Garoufalidis–Scholze–Wheeler–Zagier and the packet-level fields), whose key claims the reviewer re-checked (PARI for the eigenspace convention; the rendered GSWZ pages for (21) and (24)). Sources read: CGZ arXiv v3 §§1–7 (hash confirmed), Hutchinson arXiv v4 in full (hash confirmed), GSWZ arXiv v2 §§1.3–1.5, 2.1, 3, 5.1–5.3 (hash confirmed), Weibel's K-book IV–V. Outcome: 17 nodes corrected, 50 added, 1 deleted (HB.2's bundled bar-cycles node); 42 baseline declarations, each confirmed in the pinned index; every test has a kind; 30 source issues recorded (the packet had none). Main corrections: (1) false statements: the Bloch conventions differ by elementary abelian 2-groups, one way, not 'two- and six-primary' groups in both directions; the Remark 1.3 excerpt reversed the exponent law (R_(ζ^k) = R_ζ^(k^−1)), which would give the χ-eigenspace; the Chern-class target is the multiplicative group, not the units, and needs N odd; the Bott element lies in K₂(R; ℤ/N); GSWZ (21) has p/x, not p·x (with p·x no section exists), and (24) is a product in the Habiro ring of R[1/γ], not a ratio over R/γ; the local-picture node contradicted GSWZ Theorem 2; (2) library: PowerSeries.subst needs nilpotence, so the substitution is HabiroCyclotomicCompletions HC.3's re-expansion on PowerSeries.eval₂Hom; Mathlib's autToPow is the cyclotomic character the packet planned again; (3) closure: CGZ §3 (c_ζ, Lemmas 3.1, 3.3–3.5, Proposition 2.12, Theorem 1.5), CGZ §§2 and 4–5 (the descent to R_ζ, the KMS identity, the local maps, Theorem 1.6), Hutchinson's argument, GSWZ's compatible roots, the p-completed ring, the class decomposition, Theorems 1 and 2 and Proposition 1.5 had no nodes and are decomposed; (4) ownership: the Bloch conventions are K3BlochGroups V.3–V.6's, the Frobenius lift HabiroRings HR.1's, and nine misdirected or reversed requests (V.1, V.2, M.3 for HB.1, H.2, HR.5, HC.6, ...) are replaced. The exported units are GSWZ's ε_m = c_(ζ_m)² for every m. The refinement R_ζ = c_ζ² needs CGZ Theorem 7.4, proved only through HabiroNahmSeries HB.4, which requires HB.2: it is a gap with a restructure proposal, and the sign of the scalar depends on conventions the sources do not fix (gap). Source issues include false stated results of GSWZ (Definition 1.3's shape breaks Theorem 1 for ξ = 0; Remark 1.2 as indexed; footnote 1's φ_m) and of CGZ (§3.5's count for 3 | n; S depending on n). No stage-level or node-level cycle. Coverage: all four stages partial, with 10 gaps and 14 requests. The packet is accepted: every node is corrected or added, every baseline citation is confirmed, and the open points are recorded.
